description:

title: Walk & Talk Pakuranga: Conversations that Matter
description:
Sick of loud bars, awkward small talk, and surface-level chats?
I am too.

Let’s do something low-key - but *real*.

**🌿 Walk & Talk** \- a casual\, open\-invite stroll with people who enjoy movement\, connection\, and actual conversation\.

No agenda, no pressure, and no hierarchies.

Just walking. Talking. Sharing thoughts. Or simply listening. Flat surface - energy spent on the talk, not the terrain.

Bring your water bottle & hat. Also bring your thoughts, your awkwardness - it’s all welcome.

The event language is English, but you are welcome to use other languages when chatting with others.

📅 **Date & Time:** Saturday, August 15, 1 pm
**📍 Meeting Spot:** Rotary Reserve (96 Pakuranga Road, Pakuranga, Auckland 2010)
**🚶‍♂️ Route:** Pakuranga Rotary Path
**🐢 Pace:** Chill
**💬 Vibe:** Honest, warm, thoughtful

Drop me a message if you’re curious - or just show up 🙂

In case of difficulty finding the group, check the live location - it will be posted when the walk starts!

If you want to share your ride coming to the event, write so in the comments!

Support Walk&Talk on Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/Walks_and_Talks](https://www.patreon.com/Walks_and_Talks?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAYnJpZBExc2lteWZtMlBTV3RwcnN4cwEec_FgP2pKgPFHgNCTls9jGUWLeJWhDVAiDc7CtkDKtscEr9xpw-7ZeP3djqQ_aem_s7hOYz9R94P0t1QyeocFqg)

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please use the following link to pre-register for Xero Venue before arriving** [https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/myweaHurOU55lj2S](https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/myweaHurOU55lj2S).
* **Organisers will be at the building entrance to bring everyone to the venue.**
* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: Shipping software as a Junior without burning out by Enry Villamizar**
Stepping into software engineering is exciting, but navigating the steep learning curve alongside deliverable deadlines can easily lead to early-career fatigue. In this talk, you will learn actionable strategies for shipping production-ready code confidently without sacrificing well-being. From setting clear boundaries and managing workload expectations to building sustainable dev habits.

**A bit about Enry:**

* Enry is a Senior Software Developer driven by solving real-world business problems through smart internal software, such as building Whites Powersports’ warehouse system and Wireless Nation’s dashboard. A huge fan of video games and AI, he cares deeply about keeping development work sustainable, efficient, and burnout-free.

**Talk 2: Beyond the Prompt: Becoming a Better Developer in the Age of AI by Keith Patton**
AI tools can help junior developers produce working code faster than ever, but speed is not the same as engineering competence.
In this talk, he will share practical lessons from using AI coding tools and agentic development workflows in real software teams. He will cover where AI is genuinely useful, where it can create false confidence, and how developers can use it without outsourcing their understanding or judgement.

title: Demystifying Git
description:
**Topic**
Many of us use git for our day to day work, but do we really know whats going on? Today we will peek under the hood and get an idea of how git works under the covers. By understanding some of the git internals, we will be better equipped to recover when things go wrong (hello merge hell). No matter if you’re a beginner or an expert, there will be something you can use to improve your workflow.

**Agenda**
5:30 - Start of pizza and networking
6:00 - Demystifying Git
7:15 - Finish

Please make sure to register for the event as we need to provide contact details to Microsoft for security purposes. Registration will close 48 hours prior to the event to provide enough time to send out the access passes for in-person attendees, but you can [join online](https://aka.ms/aotearoanzgithub/stream) on the day.

If you have a topic you'd like to present (or hear about) please reach out, or create an idea in our [GitHub Ideas discussion board](https://github.com/orgs/NZ-GitHub-UG/discussions/categories/ideas).

title: Beyond the Chat Window: Building a Real AI Workspace
description:
This session looks at what it takes to move beyond a single chat window and build a genuine AI workspace – a considered set of tools, habits, and workflows that support the way you actually work and live.

We'll map the landscape by category rather than by brand, so you can understand what each type of tool is for, where the boundaries between them sit, and how they fit together into something coherent.

The focus is practical and aimed at professionals, builders, operators, and anyone who has accumulated a scattering of AI subscriptions without a sense of how they connect – team leads and those setting direction for others will also find plenty to take away.

We'll explore-

* The categories that make up an AI workspace – conversational assistants, coding and agentic tools, automation and orchestration, knowledge capture, research and search, generation of images, audio and video, and where each genuinely earns its place.
* Choosing between frontier models, specialised tools, and local options – the trade-offs in capability, cost, privacy, and control.
* Connecting your tools to your context – files, notes, calendars, email, and codebases, and what changes when AI can actually see your work.
* Techniques that separate casual use from serious use – prompting patterns, structured context, reusable instructions, and knowing when to hand off a task versus do it yourself.
* Automation and agents – identifying which recurring work is worth automating, and recognising the tasks where supervision still matters more than speed.
* Extending the workspace into life beyond work – planning, learning, health, finances, household logistics, and creative projects.
* The cost of complexity – tool sprawl, subscription creep, fragile workflows, and how to keep a stack small enough to actually maintain.
* Privacy, data boundaries, and trust – deciding what you're willing to put where, and building sensible defaults.
